notes: THE FOUR NET WORTH HEADLINES NOW OPEN THEIR OWN BREAKDOWN, matching the account tiles on the Journal. A figure that cannot be taken apart has to be taken on trust, and every reconciliation problem found in this app began exactly there. Net worth lists liquidity, non-liquid assets, any property bought inside a scenario and the loan outstanding against it, then debts as a negative. Liquidity lists cash and savings plus each instrument marked liquid, and says plainly that property and locked instruments are excluded by design. Non-liquid lists the instruments NOT marked liquid. Debts lists each liability account's outstanding balance plus every EMI instalment still scheduled, noting that EMIs sit outside liability accounts so the two do not overlap. On the current month the liquidity panel labels its cash line as live, since that figure is anchored to the real savings balance rather than the projected chain. COMPONENTS ARE CAPTURED WHERE THE CARD IS COMPUTED, not recalculated by the panel. A panel that recomputes is a second implementation and will drift; this one reports the same arithmetic the card used. As a backstop it sums its own rows and, if they fall more than a rupee from the headline, says so on screen and calls it a fault worth reporting, rather than quietly displaying a total that does not add up. VERIFIED: all four open, every breakdown reconciles exactly to its headline with no drift warning, and liquidity plus non-liquid assets minus debts equals net worth to the rupee. The modal shell is shared with the account ledger, and the Edit account button is correctly hidden for breakdowns and restored for accounts. Regression passing: instrument cross-page mismatch zero, account delta mismatches zero, Projection-to-Dashboard zero, Decisions-to-chain zero, no page errors.
